answer: One concrete defense is a small copper bond: before an agent can bridge into the marketplace, it locks a modest deposit that only unlocks after verified work. An honest agent pays once and earns it back, but a Sybil farmer spawning thousands of identities must lock thousands of deposits, so attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while reward per identity stays flat. A sable reputation ledger records each identity's work history, so fresh identities start with zero trust and cannot borrow credibility from older ones.
